facts.raw_span: A 41-year-old man presented with a long-standing history of left plantar heel pain
he underwent extensive physiotherapy for presumed plantar fasciitis and tight gastrocnemius muscles
treatment with anti-inflammatory and analgesic medications
two separate surgical releases (endoscopic plantar fascia release and minimally invasive gastrocnemius release) with only temporary relief
he reported recurrent heel pain upon return to work
he walked with an antalgic gait
the gastrocnemius remained tight with a positive Silfverskiöld test
non-specific tenderness over the plantar aspect of the calcaneus at the insertion of the plantar fascia
Weight-bearing dorsoplantar and lateral radiographs of the foot demonstrated normal bony relationships with no fractures, lesions, or signs of arthritis
Magnetic resonance imaging of the left foot showed no thickening of the plantar fascia and no signal alteration in adjacent soft tissues or bone marrow
a pedunculated bony protrusion arising from the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus, measuring approximately 1.1 cm × 0.9 cm
